title: The amazing weirdness of Tom Cruise
gist: Critic James Oliver argues that Tom Cruise's 'weirdness' is what has kept him at the top of Hollywood for 40 years since Top Gun, and that the critical and commercial flop of Alejandro González Iñárritu's 'Digger' is unlikely to end his career. Upcoming Days of Thunder 2 or a move into directing could quickly restore his standing.

insights.claim: Forty years after Top Gun, Tom Cruise has stayed at the top longer than Golden Age stars such as James Stewart, John Wayne or Bette Davis, with only Clint Eastwood reigning longer.
insights.so_what: Rare star longevity underpins bankability of franchise film assets tied to Cruise.
insights.quote: he’s been at the top—the very top—for longer than any Golden Age Hollywood star managed
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: Oliver argues Cruise's repeated ability to extend his appeal to new generations of filmgoers reflects unusual savvy and determination rather than just looks.
insights.so_what: Audience renewal is the key driver of long-run value for talent-led entertainment IP.
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: Unlike most A-listers, Cruise actively sought out auteur directors such as Kubrick, Spielberg, Mann and Paul Thomas Anderson, even taking near three years out for Eyes Wide Shut.
insights.so_what: Prestige collaborations helped sustain critical credibility alongside blockbusters.
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: Oliver credits Cruise as producer for making Mission: Impossible just about the most reliable movie franchise of recent years.
insights.so_what: Star-producer control can be a source of franchise consistency for studios.
insights.quote: Mission: Impossible has been just about the most reliable movie franchise of recent years
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: On Top Gun: Maverick, Cruise insisted on extensive reshoots after being unhappy with original footage, and the film grossed over a billion dollars with laudatory reviews.
insights.so_what: Quality-control investment by star-producers can pay off at billion-dollar box-office scale.
insights.quote: The overwhelming response—a billion-dollar-plus gross and laudatory reviews—was ample vindication.
insights.speaker: James Oliver

themes.theme: Digger flop and what comes next

insights.claim: Digger, Cruise's collaboration with Alejandro González Iñárritu intended as an Oscar vehicle, has been roasted by critics and failed to find an audience, his first flop in years.
insights.so_what: Prestige pivots by ageing action stars carry real commercial risk for studios.
insights.quote: Digger has been roasted by the critics and hasn’t found an audience
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: At 64, Cruise has hinted his action days may be winding down, as doing his own stunts becomes physically harder.
insights.so_what: Ageing of a key franchise star is a succession risk for action-film IP.
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: Oliver predicts one flop will not end Cruise's career, and that Top Gun: Maverick-sized business for Days of Thunder 2 would quickly erase Digger's memory.
insights.so_what: Days of Thunder 2 performance is the next signal for Cruise-driven box office.
insights.quote: it will take more than one flop to put The Cruiser on the canvas
insights.speaker: James Oliver

insights.claim: Cruise may yet move into directing, a long-trailed ambition that Oliver considers an enticing prospect given his taste and quality control.
insights.so_what: A directing pivot would reshape how Cruise-linked projects are packaged and financed.
insights.speaker: James Oliver
